page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It runs on the 64-bit arm64 architecture, utilizing AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance provides 32 physical cores with a dedicated 1:1 core-to-thread mapping, yielding 32 dedicated vCPUs with zero multithreading contention. Cache provisioning features 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, backed by 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server contains no integrated local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures alongside a 67 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark analysis highlights top-tier capabilities in memory throughput and multi-threaded processing. Large-block memory tests show read bandwidth reaching 391.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 185.65 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top decile. In compute benchmarks, it registers a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,681.0 and achieves strong results in Clang software compilation (49,127.0) and PassMark physics calculations (9,253.33). Database and I/O-intensive performance remain strong, as demonstrated by PassMark database operations scoring 47,341.83, Redis SET throughput exceeding 67 million operations per second, and static web serving reaching 73.17 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing across stress-ng and Geekbench falls within the median category, and text generation speeds for large language models show lower relative performance.

The qualitative efficiency of the instance stems from its dedicated physical core layout, which avoids resource contention common in hyperthreaded processors, coupled with extensive memory bandwidth. The absence of local disk drives requires external storage configurations, which makes storage performance dependent on network routing. Standard x86 vector capabilities such as AVX-512 are not present on this ARM-based chip, though hardware AES encryption is active. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation workflows, high-throughput caching layers, distributed web serving, and memory-sensitive compute workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 32 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured with a single thread per physical core, the instance provides 32 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Networking reaches a 67 Gbps baseline, with no discrete GPUs and no bundled local storage. Performance benchmarks place this platform in the top tier for multi-core Geekbench processing, PassMark database tasks, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 391.76 GB/sec. Although single-core metrics and LLM generation speeds remain in the average tier, the lack of hyperthreaded thread-sharing offers predictable multi-core execution. The instance is structured for distributed web tiers, software compilation, Redis in-memory caches, and compute tasks requiring elevated memory bandwidth.
